findings.title: Compile cache is not keyed on primary_level — a different requested level silently returns the cached level's artifact, corrupting checkpoint provenance
findings.evidence: One cache file per experiment dir (`_cache_artifact_path` = `<dir>/.compiled/universe.msgpack`), freshness compared only on config_hash / provenance_id / config_mtime — `primary_level` is not in the key and is not stored for comparison. PROVEN: after caching `configs/default_curriculum` with `primary_level='L0_0_minimal'`, compiling with `primary_level='L2_partial_observability'` and `use_cache=True` returned top-level `action_schema_hash=b8c4948d605f` (== `all_levels['L0_0_minimal'].action_schema_hash`) instead of L2's `63b969e265a2` (confirmed by the same compile with `use_cache=False`). The runtime env is unaffected because `vectorized_env.py:104` selects `metadata_for_level(level_name)`, but `training/checkpoint_utils.py:34-42` stamps `observation_dim`, `action_dim`, `observation_field_uuids`, `drive_hash` and `vfs_hash` from the corrupted top-level fields and :79-141 re-validates against them. It fires on the documented curriculum workflow: `demo/runner.py:112` and `demo/live_inference.py:293` call compile() with `use_cache` defaulting to True, so training L0 then L1 in the same pack stamps L1 checkpoints with L0's provenance.

findings.title: All universe unit-test fixtures are single-level packs, making the entire multi-level / primary-level code path unreachable by the unit suite
findings.evidence: `configs/test/model_config` -> only `L0_test`; `configs/test/effects_smoke` -> only `L0_effects`; `configs/simple` -> only `L0_simple`; `configs/reference/model_pack` -> only `L0_demo`. findings.title: Broad except around cache load misattributes user YAML errors to the cache

findings.title: Cache fingerprint is computed twice on the warm path, re-walking and re-normalising every YAML file

findings.title: Affordance effect extraction is a silent string-parsing heuristic

subsystem: SG2-vfs — Variable & Feature System + VFS Transition Compiler (src/townlet/vfs/)

completeness.evidence: Runtime half is complete end-to-end: VariableRegistry allocates 9 scopes (registry.py:452-475), the observation vector is assembled entirely from VFS state (environment/observation_encoder.py:23-45, 122-131), and 5 of 9 VTC families execute through VTCTransitionRunner (vfs/transition_schedule.py:104-108, driven from vectorized_env.py:995, 1061, 1128, 1140, 1146). Declarative half is stubbed: universe/compilers/actions.py:204-205 hardcodes reads=()/writes=() so VTCActionWriteProgram (vtc.py:395-931) always compiles zero rules; compile_vtc_affordance_occupancy (vtc.py:2176-2192) has zero production callers; `transition_rules.yaml` (raw_configs_v21.py:217-227) exists in zero packs (`find configs -name transition_rules.yaml` returns nothing); shipped packs configs/{default_curriculum,simple,aspatial_test,L5_multi_agent}/vfs_profiles.yaml declare 0 global + 0 agent variables. ~700 LOC (dynamic_needs.py 159, generalisation.py 450, relational.py 61, communication.py 27) is exported from vfs/__init__.py:10-28 with no production consumer.

correctness.evidence: No wrong-value defect proven. Access control is really enforced (registry.py:512-514 read, 546-548 write, 516-521 agent_private, 577-579 engine bypass path). Fail-loud discipline is consistent: unknown phase raises (transition_graph.py:58-63), unknown residue target raises (transition_schedule.py:287-291), unsized scope raises (registry.py:477-482), unknown state variable raises (transition_schedule.py:277). The real contract inconsistencies are silent-no-op rather than wrong-math: environment.yaml `normalization` is required and cross-validated (config/environment_config.py:103, compilers/observation.py:502-528 rejects missing and rejects method 'none') yet never applied to any tensor; and load_variables_reference_config raises 'variables_reference.yaml is required but not found' (schema.py:543) while raw_configs_v21.py:206-207 treats the file as optional and 14 of 25 packs omit it.

specification.evidence: The phase graph is the only explicit ordering spec and it is only half honoured: DEFAULT_TRANSITION_PHASES (transition_graph.py:7-26) declares 18 phases, but VTCTransitionRunner.run_phases dispatches only 5 rule families (transition_schedule.py:104-108). Modulations (vtc.py:2454 phase='apply_modulations'), affordance gates (vtc.py:2744), interaction progress (vtc.py:2536, 2557) and reward components (vtc.py:2038-2140) carry a `phase` that no handler reads — yet those phases are hashed into transition_graph_hash (schema_hashes.py:56-90), making a decorative field look normative. There is no written spec for the write ABI's semantics (what 'claim_if_free' vs 'capacity_claim' guarantee), only the implementation at vtc.py:560-620. Behaviour is the spec for most of vtc.py.

test_signal.evidence: Real behavioural assertions, not tautologies: tests/test_townlet/unit/vfs/ holds ~250 tests with concrete numeric/tensor assertions (test_registry.py 45 tests/71 asserts, incl. genuine PermissionError paths at :81, :429, :451, :524). tests/test_townlet/integration/test_vtc_transition_schedule_runtime.py:47-74 is a true YAML->compile->step->assert test (writes transition_rules.yaml, asserts trust moves 0.5 -> 0.6 while baseline stays 0.5) plus a negative case at :77-83 and an architectural-invariant test at :85-98. The gap is coverage direction, not assertion quality: test_vtc_action_writes.py (607 lines, 14 tests) exercises the write engine only via Python-constructed WriteSpec (:42-50), and test_observation_builder.py:119-156 verifies all 10 normalization kinds of a function with no production caller. No test asserts that every declared config surface is reachable, which is why the inertness survived.

tests/test_townlet/integration/test_vtc_transition_schedule_runtime.py in full. :47-74 is the only true YAML->compile->step->assert test in the subsystem (writes transition_rules.yaml, asserts trust moves 0.5->0.6 while the baseline pack stays 0.5, and asserts the hashes diverge). :77-83 covers the negative case. :85-98 asserts vectorized_env.py contains no domain tokens ('trust','reputation','faction','institution') — an architectural-invariant test that mechanically enforces the declarative boundary. Use this file as the template for the missing per-surface end-to-end tests.

The layering discipline of the package. Every import across src/townlet/vfs/*.py resolves to townlet.vfs, townlet.world.expression or townlet.config — zero imports from townlet.universe or townlet.environment. VFS is a true leaf layer with no cycles, which is why the repairs below are local rather than architectural.

VFSProfileCompiler dependency resolution (src/townlet/vfs/profiles.py:74-270): networkx dependency graph over expression references, topological ordering, explicit CircularDependencyError, and type checking against a bar/VFS schema. Paired with the mark-and-sweep evaluator (evaluator.py:120-150), which refuses to run without explicit marks rather than silently evaluating everything and expands marks transitively through the dependency map — a good fail-loud default.

TransitionPhaseGraph (src/townlet/vfs/transition_graph.py). Small, frozen, validates non-empty/non-duplicate phases, raises on unknown phase names, and emits a deterministic canonical payload for hashing. The concept is right; only its dispatch coverage needs finishing.

findings.title: Action-write ABI is unreachable from any config: compiler hardcodes writes=()
findings.evidence: build_runtime_action_space emits `reads=(), writes=()` for every action with no branch that could populate them. Consequently compile_vtc_action_writes_with_phase_graph (transition_schedule.py:211) compiles zero rules in every pack, and VTCActionWriteProgram (vtc.py:395-931) — 550 lines implementing 11 composition modes, capacity claiming, event append, priority resolution and affordance occupancy — is dead in production. `grep -rn 'WriteSpec' src/townlet` shows no construction site outside the schema itself. This is the flagship declarative surface of the transition compiler.

findings.title: Required, cross-validated observation normalization never affects any tensor
findings.evidence: environment.yaml must declare `normalization: {method, range, ...}` per variable — the compiler raises on a missing block and explicitly rejects `method: none` (observation.py:504-513, 523-528). The converted NormalizationSpec is attached to VariableDef (observation.py:431,467) and VFSObservationField (observation.py:383). apply_normalization has zero callers in src/. Both observation paths bypass it: build_vfs_observation concatenates raw registry tensors (observation_builder.py:333-360) and _build_vfs_agent_observation_field uses only source_variable and shape (observation_encoder.py:68-93). The only consumer is compute_observation_schema_hash (schema_hashes.py:153).

findings.title: transition_rules.yaml is the sole VTC authoring surface, parses one key, and exists in zero packs
findings.evidence: The loader reads only `social_residue`; all other rule families are unreachable from it. `find configs -name transition_rules.yaml` returns nothing across all 25 packs, so no shipped universe demonstrates or exercises the declarative transition surface. Its only exercise is a file written to tmp_path by tests/test_townlet/integration/test_vtc_transition_schedule_runtime.py:23-45.

findings.title: Affordance occupancy/capacity engine has no production caller; L5's occupied_by is never written
findings.evidence: compile_vtc_affordance_occupancy and _with_phase_graph are called only from tests/test_townlet/unit/vfs/test_vtc_affordance_occupancy.py:68,88. The L5 pack declares `occupied_by` with scope=affordance and writable_by=[engine, vtc], and `grep -rn 'occupied_by' src/townlet` returns nothing — the variable is allocated, folded into vfs_hash, and permanently frozen at its default.

findings.title: Three of nine declared variable scopes cannot be instantiated from config
findings.evidence: group/zone/message scopes size from num_groups/num_zones/num_message_slots, and _positive_extent raises 'must be positive' when they are 0. VectorizedHamletEnv constructs VariableRegistry passing only variables, num_agents, device, max_items, num_affordances, item_profiles, leaving all three at their 0 defaults. pair_storage_mode/pair_edges are also never passed, so sparse pair storage (registry.py:459-461) is likewise unreachable.

findings.title: Doc asserts action writes are live and lists all 11 composition modes as current
findings.evidence: Line 76 states the transition compiler consumes 'Action writes from ActionConfig.writes'; lines 257-270 enumerate overwrite/additive_delta/multiplicative_modifier/min/max/clamp/priority_write/last_write_wins/claim_if_free/capacity_claim/append_event as 'Current composition modes'. Contradicted by universe/compilers/actions.py:205. This is the most recent and otherwise most accurate VFS document (2026-05-16), which makes the claim maximally believable to an author.

findings.title: Phase field is decorative for four of nine rule families yet is hashed as world physics
findings.evidence: run_phases dispatches five handlers only (_run_action_writes, _run_passive_depletions, _run_threshold_cascades, _run_state_residue, _run_terminal_conditions). Modulations compile with phase='apply_modulations', gates with 'compute_action_legality_masks', interaction progress with 'advance_interaction_progress'/'apply_completion_bonuses', rewards with 'compute_rewards' — none has a handler. Modulations actually execute at vectorized_env.py:704 during action execution, ahead of the 'apply_passive_depletion' phase their declared index follows. canonical_transition_graph_schema (schema_hashes.py:56-90) folds all of these phases into transition_graph_hash, presenting an ordering contract the runner does not implement.

findings.title: vfs_profiles.yaml semantic_type is discarded; the one reader uses a name-substring heuristic and is itself dead
findings.evidence: semantic_type is a validated Literal on all three profile kinds (config/vfs_profiles_config.py:29,137,247) and survives into CompiledVariable (profiles.py:36) and the cache (compiled.py:788,816). The observation compiler hardcodes semantic_type='custom' for environment and profile-derived fields. vfs_to_observation_spec:72 calls _semantic_from_name(field.id) instead of reading field.semantic_type, and returns values ('position','meter') outside the declared Literal set; that function has no caller in src/ (only tests/test_townlet/unit/universe/test_vfs_adapter.py:25,38).

findings.title: Declared access control on profile variables is overwritten by the compiler
findings.evidence: _compiled_profile_var_to_variable_def returns VariableDef(readable_by=['agent','engine'], writable_by=['engine'], description=f'{scope} VFS variable from vfs_profiles.yaml') for every compiled profile variable. The registry enforces these lists strictly (registry.py:512-514, 546-548), so the enforcement is real but the policy is not authorable for the one file every pack ships.

findings.title: ~700 LOC of orphaned research scaffold exported from the public API
findings.evidence: dynamic_needs.py has zero consumers anywhere — src/ or tests/ (`grep -rn 'dynamic_needs|DynamicNeed'`). generalisation.py, relational.py and communication.py are imported only by vfs/__init__.py:12-28 and by unit tests (test_generalisation_harness.py, test_relational_variables.py, test_message_variables.py). Under the zero-backwards-compatibility contract these are deletions, not assets; the canonical helpers in relational.py/communication.py additionally target scopes the environment cannot size (see the scope finding).

findings.title: No shipped curriculum pack declares a single global or agent VFS variable
findings.evidence: Parsing all 21 vfs_profiles.yaml files: default_curriculum has 0 global / 0 agent / 1 item profile with 0 variables; simple and L5_multi_agent have 0/0/0; aspatial_test has 0/0/1-empty. Only configs/reference/model_pack (1 global, 2 agent, 2 item vars) and test packs exercise the profile compiler, evaluator, mark-and-sweep and item-observation paths. findings.evidence: 607 lines / 14 tests exercise the write engine solely through Python-constructed WriteSpec objects; test_observation_builder verifies all 10 normalization kinds of a function with zero production callers. The assertions are strong but they certify reachability that does not exist — no test asserts that a declared schema field is producible from YAML, which is why every finding above survived a 2942-test suite.

findings.title: vtc.py is a 2990-line module concentrating nine rule families
findings.evidence: One file holds 9 source Protocols, 11 compiled dataclasses, 9 runtime Program classes and 18 compile entry points. Wiring a single family into the runner requires coordinated edits in vtc.py, transition_schedule.py (add handler), schema_hashes.py (canonical payload) and vectorized_env.py (call site) — four files for what the architecture presents as one declarative addition.

findings.evidence: load_variables_reference_config raises FileNotFoundError('variables_reference.yaml is required but not found in {config_dir}') while the v2.1 loader guards it with `if variables_reference_path.exists()`. 11 of 25 packs contain the file and none of them is default_curriculum. subsystem: SG3-config-dto (src/townlet/config/ — Pydantic DTO layer, no-defaults enforcement, brain_config.py / Brain-as-Code layer 2)

correctness.evidence: No mis-validation found: every validator I traced computes the constraint it claims (bars_v2_config.py:62-67, 94-103; training_v2_config.py:108-147, 266-284; brain_config.py:240-252, 296-330, 349-350, 429-451). Three provable code-level defects: (1) unreachable validator training_v2_config.py:368-373 — enabled_affordances is a required non-Optional list[str], so Pydantic rejects null before the validator runs; (2) load_training_v2_config (training_v2_config.py:428-437) reads only data['training'|'run_metadata'|'recording'] and silently ignores every other ROOT key, defeating extra=forbid at the file level — demonstrated by tests/test_townlet/unit/config/test_config_pack_factory.py:24-33 which injects a root 'environment:' key into training.yaml and the pack still loads; (3) missing extra=forbid on effects_config.py:214 (EffectDefinitionConfig), effects_config.py:250 (EffectsConfig) and vfs_config.py:8 (VariablesReferenceConfig, no model_config at all), so misspelled keys in effects.yaml / variables_reference.yaml are silently dropped.

specification.evidence: The DTO docstrings are the only spec and they describe field *syntax*, never whether the field binds at runtime. Nothing states which of the 322 declared fields the engine actually reads, and the schemas actively assert the opposite: training_v2_config.py:106-126 attaches two cross-field validators to min_size, and brain_config.py:130 validates LSTM num_layers ge=1 le=4, both of which are ignored by the runtime. Where a field is honestly labelled inert (environment_config.py:27 range_type: 'Metadata only for UI') no UI reads it either. Config-level invariants that should be specified are absent: nothing anywhere requires experiment.curriculum_levels to match the levels/ directory contents.

test_signal.evidence: 139 tests pass in 2.4s across tests/test_townlet/unit/config/ (~1.4k LOC) + tests/test_townlet/unit/agent/test_brain_config.py (988 LOC, 48 tests, 24 pytest.raises). subsystem: SG4-environment-dac (src/townlet/environment/ — VectorizedHamletEnv tick loop, DACEngine, action masking, affordance engine, POMDP observation encoding)

completeness.evidence: The tick loop is built end-to-end and executes: vectorized_env.py:972-1113 runs actions -> VTC action writes -> passive depletion -> threshold cascades -> effects -> VFS evaluation -> terminal conditions -> rewards -> observations, all delegating to compiled VTC programs (_run_vtc_transition_phases, vectorized_env.py:1152-1175). All 9 DAC extrinsic strategy types in the Literal at config/drive_as_code.py:181-192 have real implementations (dac_engine.py:157,186,219,247,278,313,347,379,408) and all 11 shaping types at config/drive_as_code.py:292-565 are implemented (dac_engine.py:463-814). Observation encoding is fully spec-driven (observation_encoder.py:24-45). Holes are specific rather than pervasive: two strategies are self-declared stubs (dac_engine.py:347-349 'Full implementation would have operation field (min/max/mean/product)' but hardcodes torch.min at :371; dac_engine.py:408-410 'Full implementation would compose multiple sub-strategies'), custom actions are structurally unable to do anything (below), and there is a silent zero-reward fallback for unrecognised strategy types at dac_engine.py:452-456.

correctness.evidence: Four provable defects. (1) The LIVE instant-interaction path drops safety the DEAD one has: _handle_instant_interactions calls affordance_engine.apply_interaction (action_executor.py:275-280 -> affordance_engine.py:396-450), which deducts costs at :432-435 and returns at :450 with NO torch.clamp; the orphaned apply_instant_interaction (affordance_engine.py:154-211) does the identical work but validates interaction_type (:177-181), checks all-meter affordability (:186-189) and clamps to [0,1] (:208-209). apply_instant_interaction has zero callers in src/. (2) Affordability is checked only against a bar literally named 'money' (vectorized_env.py:628 self.money_idx = meter_name_to_index.get('money'); action_executor.py:185-187, 269-272) and get_affordance_cost returns only the first cost whose meter == 'money' (affordance_engine.py:374-377), so an affordance costing energy or credits is never gated. (3) Terminal agents get an all-False action mask (action_mask_builder.py:206-207) but the executor never consults dones — action_executor.py:27-29 applies substrate movement to every agent including dead ones, and :60 deducts movement cost from them. (4) Boundary masking hardcodes hard walls (action_mask_builder.py:130-179) and never reads substrate.boundary, contradicting the wrap/bounce/sticky modes implemented in substrate/grid3d.py:105-131 and gridnd.py:82-93; the abstract Substrate.get_valid_neighbors, documented at substrate/base.py:233 as 'Used for action masking (boundary checks)', has zero callers in src/.

specification.evidence: Behaviour is the only spec, and the code says so in its own comments. dac_engine.py:347-349 and :408-410 declare themselves simplified against an unwritten fuller contract. The 16-stage tick ordering exists only as inline numbered comments in vectorized_env.py:990-1103, and those numbers are already inconsistent — stage '6.' appears twice (:1085 rewards, :1099 time-of-day) and stages 3.5/3.6/5.1/5.5 are interpolations, so there is no canonical stage list to check an implementation against. The retirement bonus is a magic +1.0 literal with no config surface (vectorized_env.py:1086). The step() docstring still says 'actions: [num_agents] tensor of actions (0-4)' (vectorized_env.py:983) against a >=8-action space. ComposedActionSpace's own docstring says 'substrate_action_count: Number from substrate (6 for Grid2D)' (action_builder.py:19) while grid2d.py:159-300 emits INTERACT and WAIT as substrate actions too — and action_executor.py:143 depends on INTERACT being inside substrate_mask, so the docstring being wrong is load-bearing.

test_signal.evidence: 353 of 354 unit tests in tests/test_townlet/unit/environment/ pass (verified: PYTORCH_JIT=0 uv run pytest -> '353 passed, 1 skipped'), with 700+ assertions that mostly check real numbers, not smoke. test_movement_mask_bug.py:34-60 asserts exact energy deltas derived from the compiled passive-depletion program; test_action_masking.py carries 91 assertions on mask semantics. The named gap is the product-critical one: every DACEngine test constructs DriveAsCodeConfig as a Python object (test_dac_engine.py:6-16, 57-71) — zero tests load a drive.yaml, so the YAML-to-behaviour path that IS the product promise is untested, which is exactly how composition.normalize/clip stayed inert. Second gap: tests exercise dead code as if live — tests/test_townlet/unit/test_action_builder.py (9 instantiations of the zero-caller ActionSpaceBuilder), test_load_global_actions.py (a file that no longer exists anywhere under configs/), and test_affordance_engine.py:306-360 tests _check_affordability, reachable only from the dead apply_instant_interaction. NOTE: a full-suite run on this machine shows 37 failures, but these are entirely a broken local CUDA toolchain (nvrtc: failed to open libnvrtc-builtins.so.13.0) hit once torch.jit.script kernels in vfs/vtc_kernels.py:8-67 warm up into NNC fusion; PYTORCH_JIT=0 makes all 37 pass. This is not a test-quality signal and I have not scored it as one.

doc_truth.evidence: Scoped to the docs I actually opened for this subsystem. docs/config-schemas/drive_as_code.md documents a filename and root key that do not exist — the real file is levels/<level>/drive.yaml with root key 'drive:' (configs/default_curriculum/levels/L0_0_minimal/drive.yaml:1). Worse, it documents two inert fields as functional at lines 250-251: '`normalize` (bool): Apply tanh normalization to total reward' and '`clip` (dict | null): Clip total reward to {min, max} range', neither of which is read anywhere in dac_engine.py. CLAUDE.md's DAC section reproduces the same wrong filename ('drive_as_code.yaml (REQUIRED)') and wrong root key in its L0_0_minimal example, and its action-space claim 'Grid2D: 8 actions (6 substrate + INTERACT + WAIT)' contradicts grid2d.py:159-300, where INTERACT and WAIT are themselves substrate actions.

changeability.evidence: The component extraction is a facade over a god object, not a decomposition. RewardCalculator, ActionExecutor and ObservationEncoder are all constructed as `Cls(self)` (vectorized_env.py:99-101) and reach back into private env state: reward_calculator.py:31-35 calls env._get_affordance_positions, env._get_last_action_affordances, env._get_affordance_streaks, env._get_unique_affordances_used, then writes env.intrinsic_weights and env._last_reward_components at :48-49. action_executor.py:36-46 pokes env.vfs_registry._definitions directly. vectorized_env.py is still 1459 lines and re-exposes the same methods it delegated away (:1117-1119, :1209-1211) so both call paths stay live. Concretely: adding a config-driven retirement bonus means touching the env body, the DAC schema, the DAC engine and the reward facade. The hot path also depends on torch.jit.script kernels (vfs/vtc_kernels.py:8-67) with no CPU fallback or degradation guard, which is why a toolchain hiccup takes down 37 tests. Per-agent Python loops in the vectorized hot path (affordance_engine.py:628-etc _execute_affordance_effects loops `for agent_idx in torch.where(agent_mask)[0]`; action_executor.py:74-79, 92-99, 108-116) further constrain how this can be changed.

declared_but_inert.surface: stratum.yaml substrate boundary modes wrap / bounce / sticky
declared_but_inert.evidence: The schema accepts Literal['clamp','wrap','bounce','sticky'] and the substrates implement all four in apply_movement. The action mask builder never reads self.substrate.boundary — it unconditionally masks moves that would leave the grid (at_top/at_bottom/at_left/at_right, :131-134). On a `wrap` grid the author's declared toroidal topology is contradicted by the mask. The abstract hook meant for this, Substrate.get_valid_neighbors, is documented at base.py:233 as 'Used for action masking (boundary checks)' and has zero callers in src/. Every shipped config sets `boundary: clamp` (configs/default_curriculum/stratum.yaml:12 and all of configs/test/*), which is why it has never surfaced.

declared_but_inert.surface: affordances.yaml `opening_hours:` on non-temporal levels
declared_but_inert.evidence: _is_affordance_open returns True unconditionally when `not self.enable_temporal_mechanics` (vectorized_env.py:438-439), and the mask builder only calls the gate under `if self.enable_temporal_mechanics` (:187). enable_temporal_mechanics requires curriculum.active_temporal (vectorized_env.py:120-122), which is false for L0_0_minimal, L0_5_dual_resource, L1_full_observability and L2_partial_observability (configs/default_curriculum/levels/*/curriculum.yaml). Yet those levels' affordances.yaml all declare opening_hours (e.g. configs/default_curriculum/levels/L1_full_observability/affordances.yaml:9,35,59,82,...). Four of five shipped levels declare shop hours that are silently ignored.

declared_but_inert.surface: affordances.yaml `interaction_type: multi_tick` / `duration_ticks:` on non-temporal levels
declared_but_inert.evidence: _handle_interactions short-circuits to _handle_instant_interactions when `not env.enable_temporal_mechanics` (action_executor.py:163-164). Multi-tick progress is therefore coupled to the day/night cycle for no stated reason: on L0/L0.5/L1/L2 a multi_tick affordance would fire its full on_start effects instantly with duration_ticks ignored. The live instant path also never validates interaction_type (affordance_engine.py:396-450), whereas the dead sibling raises on a mismatch (affordance_engine.py:177-181). All shipped affordances are `interaction_type: instant`, so this never fires today.

declared_but_inert.surface: DAC shaping bonuses that depend on optional reward-context kwargs fail open to zero
declared_but_inert.evidence: reward_calculator.py:39-40 only injects `current_hour` when env.enable_temporal_mechanics. compute_timing_bonus returns torch.zeros when current_hour is None (dac_engine.py:674-677). So a `timing_bonus` declared in drive.yaml on a non-temporal level validates, compiles, and silently contributes exactly 0.0 forever with no warning. The same fail-open shape (`kwargs.get(...)` then return zeros) repeats at :481-484, :531-534, :576-579, :619-624 and :654-657.

declared_but_inert.surface: Unrecognised extrinsic strategy silently yields zero reward
declared_but_inert.evidence: After the nine `elif strategy.type ==` branches, _compile_extrinsic falls through to `def placeholder(...): return torch.zeros(self.num_agents, ...)` and returns it. The Literal at config/drive_as_code.py:181-192 currently covers exactly the nine implemented types so this is unreachable today — but it converts any future schema addition into a silent all-zero reward function rather than a compile error, which is the precise failure mode this product cannot afford.

authorability_gaps.capability: Give a custom action any effect at all — cost, meter change, or teleport
authorability_gaps.why_python_required: actions.yaml's CustomActionConfig accepts only name/description/enabled_by_default with extra='forbid' (config/actions_config.py:38-43). The runtime ActionConfig has costs/effects/teleport_to fields but the compiler hardcodes them empty (universe/compilers/actions.py:199-205) and the executor never reads them. The only way to make a non-movement, non-INTERACT action do something is to register it as an item custom action in Python via ItemActionHandler.custom_action_specs (consumed at action_executor.py:118-129).

authorability_gaps.capability: Use a currency bar that is not literally named 'money'
authorability_gaps.why_python_required: The affordability gate resolves a single hardcoded bar name (vectorized_env.py:628 `self.money_idx = meter_name_to_index.get('money')`) and get_affordance_cost scans only for `meter == 'money'` (affordance_engine.py:374-377). An author whose game uses 'credits', 'mana' or 'stamina' gets money_idx=None, the `if env.money_idx is not None` guard is skipped (action_executor.py:185, 269), and affordances become free. Making a different bar the currency requires editing the env.

authorability_gaps.capability: Set the episode-completion (retirement) reward
authorability_gaps.why_python_required: The retirement bonus is a bare literal in the tick loop: `rewards = torch.where(retired, rewards + 1.0, rewards)` (vectorized_env.py:1086). There is no drive.yaml field for it, so a magnitude-1.0 terminal reward is silently added to every reward function regardless of what the author's drive spec composes — including one whose per-step rewards are O(0.01) (configs/default_curriculum/levels/L0_0_minimal/drive.yaml:17 base_reward: 0.01).

authorability_gaps.capability: Normalize or clip the composed reward
authorability_gaps.why_python_required: composition.normalize and composition.clip exist in the schema (config/drive_as_code.py:602-603) and are documented as functional (docs/config-schemas/drive_as_code.md:250-251), but dac_engine.py:942 composes and returns with no tanh and no clamp. An author who needs bounded rewards must patch DACEngine.calculate_rewards.

authorability_gaps.capability: Choose the aggregation operator for the `aggregation` extrinsic strategy, or compose sub-strategies with `hybrid`
authorability_gaps.why_python_required: The engine hardcodes torch.min for aggregation and says so — 'Full implementation would have operation field (min/max/mean/product)' (dac_engine.py:347-349, operator at :371). hybrid is likewise 'simplified' with sub-strategy composition unimplemented (dac_engine.py:408-410). Neither schema exposes an operator field, so max/mean/product require editing the engine.

authorability_gaps.capability: Have a non-clamp boundary mode actually affect what the agent may do
authorability_gaps.why_python_required: wrap/bounce/sticky are honoured by substrate.apply_movement but the action mask hardcodes hard-wall semantics with no substrate consultation (action_mask_builder.py:130-179). An author declaring a toroidal world must edit ActionMaskBuilder to stop it forbidding edge-crossing moves.

authorability_gaps.capability: Use multi-tick affordances or opening hours without also enabling the day/night cycle
authorability_gaps.why_python_required: Both features are gated on enable_temporal_mechanics, which is derived from stratum.temporal_support AND curriculum.active_temporal (vectorized_env.py:120-122). action_executor.py:163-164 routes to the instant path and vectorized_env.py:438-439 short-circuits the gate. Decoupling duration from the clock requires editing the executor.

keep_these: ObservationEncoder._get_observations (src/townlet/environment/observation_encoder.py:24-45) — the observation vector is assembled purely by iterating env.observation_spec.fields and pulling each field from the VFS registry. No hardcoded field list, no positional assumptions. This is the single best realisation of 'world as code' in the subsystem and should be preserved verbatim.

The shape-validation discipline in the encoder: _ensure_agent_observation_shape (observation_encoder.py:101-109) and _build_vfs_agent_observation_field (:68-91) raise on any mismatch between compiled spec dims and produced tensor shape rather than padding or truncating. Fail-loud is exactly right for a compiler-fed runtime.

ActionMaskBuilder (src/townlet/environment/action_mask_builder.py) as a shape — stateless, constructed once with env-immutable structure, called each tick with explicit per-tick state, with a class docstring (:24-30) that states its own thread/reset contract. The boundary-mode bug is inside it but the extraction pattern is the right one and worth replicating.

The __init__ phase decomposition (vectorized_env.py:507-712) — _configure_partial_observability, _initialize_vfs_subsystem, _initialize_dac_engine, _initialize_item_subsystem, _initialize_affordance_engine, each documenting which attributes it writes and which prior phase it depends on. This is the difference between a readable 1459-line file and an unreadable one.

DACEngine._same_device (dac_engine.py:891-901) — correctly treats cuda and cuda:0 as equal instead of naive device equality. A small thing that silently prevents a class of spurious RuntimeErrors on multi-GPU boxes.

AffordanceEngine._get_meter_idx (affordance_engine.py:473-489) — raises KeyError with the offending meter name, the context ('affordance X cost'), AND the sorted list of available meters. Every config-facing lookup error in this codebase should read like this.

NullItemManager (src/townlet/environment/null_managers.py) — no-ops the lifecycle methods but raises RuntimeError on spawn_item (:41-49). A null object that fails loud on the operations that imply the subsystem should have been configured is the correct half-measure, not a fallback antipattern.

The DAC closure-factory pattern (dac_engine.py:463 create_approach_reward_fn, :500 create_completion_bonus_fn, and nine siblings) — each bonus config is captured in an explicit factory rather than a late-binding loop closure. This is the classic Python bug and someone deliberately avoided it eleven times.

torch.clamp(bar_value, min=0.0) before torch.pow in the polynomial strategy (dac_engine.py:294-296, comment 'CRIT-01: Clamp to non-negative to prevent NaN from negative^fractional') — a real bug fixed with a comment explaining the failure mode.

The reward-context threading in RewardCalculator._calculate_shaped_rewards (reward_calculator.py:30-46) — shaping context is assembled into an explicit dict and passed through VTCRewardProgram rather than the engine reaching into env state. The facade back-reaching is a problem, but this particular boundary is drawn correctly.

The explicit no-defaults raises in __init__: device is None (vectorized_env.py:88-89), missing compiled action labels (:148-149), missing experiment_name (:159-163), day_length required when temporal is active (:124-129), enabled_affordances must be an explicit list (:114-115 and env_factory.py:41-42). These enforce the no-defaults principle at the exact point an author would otherwise get silent behaviour.

findings.title: Live instant-interaction path drops the meter clamp, affordability check, and type validation that its dead sibling has
findings.evidence: apply_interaction deducts affordance costs at :432-435 and returns at :450 with no torch.clamp. The orphaned apply_instant_interaction does identical work but validates interaction_type (:177-181), runs _check_affordability across every cost meter (:186-189), and clamps to [0,1] (:208-209). grep confirms apply_instant_interaction has zero callers in src/ (only a docstring mention at :265). Failure scenario: an affordance with costs [{meter: energy, amount: 0.5}] applied to an agent at energy=0.1 — the money-only gate (action_executor.py:269-272) does not fire because the cost meter is not 'money' — yields energy=-0.4. That negative value is read this same tick by the DAC multiplicative extrinsic (dac_engine.py:157-185, reward = base * energy * health), flipping the reward sign, and is emitted in the observation vector before the next tick's passive-depletion clamp restores range. The defensive clamp already added to the polynomial strategy (dac_engine.py:294-296, 'CRIT-01: prevent NaN from negative^fractional') shows someone has already been bitten by out-of-range bars.

findings.title: drive.yaml composition block is entirely inert while docs certify it as functional
findings.evidence: CompositionConfig declares normalize, clip, log_components, log_modifiers. dac_engine.py:90-91 reads log_components/log_modifiers into attributes that nothing ever consults again; normalize and clip are never referenced anywhere. calculate_rewards composes with `total_reward = extrinsic + intrinsic + shaping_total` (:942) and returns. Failure scenario: an author sets `clip: {min: -1.0, max: 1.0}` in drive.yaml to bound an exploding shaping term; the config validates, the run proceeds, rewards are unbounded, and nothing in the logs indicates the setting was ignored. Every shipped pack sets the no-op values (configs/default_curriculum/levels/*/drive.yaml:46-47), so the field has never been exercised even accidentally. docs/config-schemas/drive_as_code.md:250-251 documents both as working.

findings.title: A custom action declared in actions.yaml cannot do anything — it is structurally a no-op
findings.evidence: CustomActionConfig (extra='forbid') permits only name, description, enabled_by_default — there is no costs, effects, delta or teleport field an author can write. The compiler hardcodes effects={}, teleport_to=None, reads=(), writes=(). In the executor, substrate_mask = actions < custom_action_start_id (:22,27) excludes custom ids from movement, item custom actions are matched by name against ItemActionHandler.custom_action_specs (:118-121), and INTERACT is matched by id (:136). Failure scenario: an author adds REST to training.enabled_actions on L0_0_minimal (it is already declared at configs/default_curriculum/actions.yaml:15-17 as 'Passive energy recovery'); the agent selects it; nothing happens — no energy recovery, no cost, no error. This is the most direct contradiction of 'build a DRL gym without writing Python' in the subsystem.

findings.title: Affordance affordability is hardcoded to a bar literally named 'money'
findings.evidence: self.money_idx = meter_name_to_index.get('money') is the only currency resolution; get_affordance_cost iterates costs and returns only the first whose meter == 'money', else 0.0. Failure scenario: an author builds a mana-based universe with bars [mana, health] and an affordance costing 0.3 mana. money_idx is None, so `if env.money_idx is not None` (action_executor.py:269) is skipped and the affordability filter never runs; get_affordance_cost returns 0.0 so the `if cost_normalized > 0` guard (:271) is also skipped. The interaction always succeeds regardless of balance, and apply_interaction then drives mana negative (see finding 1). This is domain semantics leaking into a subsystem the brief requires to be experiment-agnostic.

findings.title: Action mask hardcodes hard-wall boundaries, contradicting declared wrap/bounce/sticky substrate modes
findings.evidence: The builder computes at_top/at_bottom/at_left/at_right from grid_size and unconditionally masks off any move whose delta leaves the grid. self.substrate is held as an attribute but self.substrate.boundary is never read. The substrates implement all four modes in apply_movement (grid3d.py:105-131, gridnd.py:82-93) and the abstract hook designed for this — Substrate.get_valid_neighbors, whose docstring at base.py:233 says 'Used for action masking (boundary checks)' — has zero callers in src/. Failure scenario: an author sets `boundary: wrap` in stratum.yaml to build a toroidal world; movement would wrap correctly, but the agent at x=0 is never permitted to select LEFT, so the toroidal topology is unreachable and the declared config is silently overridden. Every shipped config sets `boundary: clamp` (configs/default_curriculum/stratum.yaml:12), which is why this has never surfaced.

findings.title: opening_hours and multi_tick interactions are silently inert on four of five shipped levels
findings.evidence: _is_affordance_open returns True unconditionally when not enable_temporal_mechanics; _handle_interactions routes to the instant path under the same condition; the mask builder only consults the gate under `if self.enable_temporal_mechanics`. enable_temporal_mechanics requires curriculum.active_temporal (vectorized_env.py:120-122), which is false for L0_0_minimal, L0_5_dual_resource, L1_full_observability and L2_partial_observability. Failure scenario: L1_full_observability's affordances.yaml declares opening_hours on all fourteen affordances (:9, :35, :59, :82, ...); the config compiles, validates, and every affordance is open 24/7 with no warning. An author debugging why their agent visits the shop at 3am has no signal that the level's temporal flag disabled the feature.

findings.title: ActionConfig's entire behavioural surface (costs, effects, teleport_to, reads, writes) is copied and hashed but never executed
findings.evidence: The DTO declares costs and effects as required-no-default fields with explicit no-defaults commentary (:37-47), plus teleport_to (:57-59), reads (:81-84) and writes (:85-88). The compiler emits effects={}, teleport_to=None, reads=(), writes=() for every action (compilers/actions.py:199-205). _build_action_space_from_runtime_artifact faithfully copies them into ActionConfig (vectorized_env.py:483-493) and vfs/schema_hashes.py:168-172 folds them into the provenance hash. No execution path reads them: movement cost comes from bars.depletion.move (action_executor.py:54-60), interaction cost from bars.depletion.interact (:139-150). The fields exist solely to make the checkpoint hash look richer than the behaviour is.

findings.title: Dead agents still move and still pay movement cost, contradicting the all-False action mask
findings.evidence: The mask builder sets action_masks[dones] = False as its final step, documented as 'Terminal agents lose all actions'. The consumer sets masked_q_values[~action_masks] = -inf then argmaxes (population/vectorized.py:568), which for an all-inf row returns index 0 — a movement action. _execute_actions never consults env.dones: substrate_mask = actions < custom_action_start_id (:27) admits the dead agent, positions are updated at :29, and movement cost is deducted at :59-60. Failure scenario: a terminated agent at step N continues drifting across the grid and depleting meters until reset, corrupting position and meter state that _get_observations and the affordance-position shaping bonuses read. Every other tick phase guards correctly with active_mask=~prev_dones (vectorized_env.py:993, 1060), so the executor is the sole inconsistency.

findings.title: DAC shaping bonuses fail open to zero when their reward-context kwarg is absent
findings.evidence: Every kwarg-dependent shaping fn does `x = kwargs.get(name)` then `if x is None: return torch.zeros(...)`. current_hour is only injected when env.enable_temporal_mechanics (reward_calculator.py:39-40). Failure scenario: an author declares a timing_bonus in L1_full_observability's drive.yaml to reward eating at midday. The DAC schema validates it (config/drive_as_code.py:477-497), the engine compiles it into shaping_fns, it is invoked every tick, and it returns exactly 0.0 forever because the level is non-temporal. No warning, no log line, no compile error. This pattern converts a configuration mistake into an invisible reward-function change.

findings.title: ActionSpaceBuilder is dead code that loads a config file which no longer exists, and has 9 tests keeping it alive
findings.evidence: grep for ActionSpaceBuilder across src/ finds only its own definition plus three stale docstring references (substrate/base.py:86, environment/action_config.py:62). The env builds its action space exclusively from the compiled runtime artifact (vectorized_env.py:476-504). ActionSpaceBuilder._load_global_custom_actions reads global_actions.yaml (:177-179) and `find configs -name global_actions.yaml` returns nothing — the file was deleted in the v2.1 migration. build() guards with `if self.global_actions_path.exists()` (:147), a silent-skip fallback that the zero-backcompat contract forbids outright. Nine test instantiations keep it green and make the subsystem look better-tested than it is.

findings.title: Two DAC extrinsic strategies are self-declared stubs with no config surface for the missing behaviour
findings.evidence: aggregation carries the comment 'Full implementation would have operation field (min/max/mean/product)' at :348-349 and then hardcodes torch.min(bar_values, dim=1).values at :371; the docstring even says 'Aggregation: reward = base + min(bars)'. hybrid says 'Full implementation would compose multiple sub-strategies' (:409-410) and instead reinterprets BarBonusConfig.center as a linear-vs-shaped switch on an epsilon test (:429-436). Failure scenario: an author selects `type: aggregation` intending a max or mean over bars — the type is accepted by the Literal at config/drive_as_code.py:181-192, no operator field exists to express the intent, and the run silently uses min. The schema advertises a family; the engine implements one member.

findings.title: The retirement bonus is a hardcoded +1.0 magic constant outside the reward specification
findings.evidence: `rewards = torch.where(retired, rewards + 1.0, rewards)  # +1 retirement bonus` is added after DACEngine has composed the full reward. drive.yaml has no field for it. Failure scenario: L0_0_minimal's drive spec uses base_reward 0.01 with bar bonuses scaled 0.5 (configs/default_curriculum/levels/L0_0_minimal/drive.yaml:17-24), so per-step rewards are O(0.01-1.0); a terminal +1.0 is therefore a dominant, undeclared terminal reward that no drive.yaml A/B test can vary or ablate. For a system whose stated purpose is letting operators A/B reward structures without code changes, a magic terminal reward outside the spec defeats the comparison.

findings.title: No test exercises the YAML-to-reward path — every DAC test builds the config in Python
findings.evidence: Every test imports DriveAsCodeConfig/ExtrinsicStrategyConfig/etc. and instantiates them directly; grep for 'yaml' and 'drive.yaml' in the file returns nothing. grep for normalize/clip/composition across the file returns only the string 'composition' in two test names about component arithmetic (:2248, :2250). Failure scenario: this is the exact mechanism by which composition.normalize/clip stayed inert through 53 tests and 963 lines of engine — the tests validate the engine against Python objects, not against what a config author can actually write, so a field that the parser accepts but the engine ignores is invisible to the whole suite. One test that loads configs/default_curriculum/levels/L0_0_minimal/drive.yaml and asserts a numeric reward would close the class.

findings.title: Tick-loop stage numbering is inconsistent and there is no canonical stage specification
findings.evidence: The tick loop is documented only by inline numbered comments, and the numbers do not form a sequence: stage '6.' appears twice — '# 6. Calculate rewards' at :1085 and '# 6. Increment time of day' at :1099 — with interpolated stages 3.5 (:1007), 3.6 (:1023), 5.1 (:1073) and 5.5 (:1080) showing where phases were retrofitted. There is no separate document or test asserting the phase order. Failure scenario: an author or agent adding a phase has no authority to consult about where effects must run relative to cascades and terminal conditions, and the only existing ordering evidence is comments that already contradict themselves. The golden-tick test (test_vectorized_env.py::TestVectorizedHamletEnvGoldenTick) asserts delegation, not stage ordering.

findings.title: Component extraction is a facade: the extracted classes hold the env and reach into its private state
findings.evidence: All three components are constructed as Cls(self) (vectorized_env.py:99-101). RewardCalculator calls four private env methods (env._get_affordance_positions, _get_last_action_affordances, _get_affordance_streaks, _get_unique_affordances_used at reward_calculator.py:32-35) and writes two private env attributes (env.intrinsic_weights, env._last_reward_components at :48-49). ActionExecutor reaches into env.vfs_registry._definitions directly (action_executor.py:36, 38, 41, 44). vectorized_env.py then re-exposes the delegated methods as thin wrappers (:1117-1119, :1209-1211) so both call paths remain live. Failure scenario: making the retirement bonus config-driven touches vectorized_env.py, the DAC schema, dac_engine.py and reward_calculator.py, and the private back-references mean no component can be unit-tested or replaced without a full env instance.

findings.title: Unrecognised extrinsic strategy compiles to a silent all-zero reward function
findings.evidence: After the nine implemented branches, _compile_extrinsic falls through to `def placeholder(meters, dones): return torch.zeros(self.num_agents, device=self.device)` and returns it. The Literal at config/drive_as_code.py:181-192 currently enumerates exactly those nine types, so it is unreachable today. Failure scenario: the moment a tenth strategy name is added to the Literal (or a subclass widens it) without an engine branch, every run using it trains against an identically-zero extrinsic reward with no error. Under the zero-backcompat contract this should be `raise ValueError(f'Unimplemented extrinsic strategy {strategy.type}')`.

findings.title: approach_reward clamps with max below min when weight is negative
findings.evidence: `bonus = weight * (1.0 - distances / max_distance)` then `bonus = torch.clamp(bonus, min=0.0, max=weight)`. ApproachRewardConfig does not constrain weight to be positive (config/drive_as_code.py:292-311). Failure scenario: an author writes a negative approach weight to create a repulsion penalty; torch.clamp with max < min silently returns max (the negative weight) for every agent regardless of distance, so the bonus becomes a constant penalty independent of position rather than a distance-shaped one. Other shaping bonuses (vfs_variable at :828-831) explicitly document negative-weight support, so this is an inconsistency within the same engine.

findings.title: DACEngine.calculate_rewards accepts step_counts and never uses it
findings.evidence: step_counts: torch.Tensor is a required positional parameter, documented in the docstring as '[num_agents] current step count', threaded from vectorized_env through VTCRewardProgram.apply (vfs/vtc.py:1771-1777) and reward_calculator.py:42. It appears nowhere in the body — no device validation, no use in any strategy or bonus. It is a required parameter on the product's central reward API that constrains nothing, and it makes the reward-backend contract look richer than it is.

findings.title: The tick loop's hot path depends on TorchScript JIT fusion with no fallback; a toolchain fault takes down 37 subsystem tests
findings.evidence: The VTC kernels the tick loop runs every step are @torch.jit.script decorated (a legacy path in torch 2.x). On this machine (torch 2.11.0+cu130, cuda available) a full run of tests/test_townlet/unit/environment/ yields '37 failed, 316 passed' with `RuntimeError: nvrtc: error: failed to open libnvrtc-builtins.so.13.0` once NNC fusion warms up; the identical run with PYTORCH_JIT=0 yields '353 passed, 1 skipped'. The failures are a broken local CUDA toolchain, not a code defect, and I have not scored them as test quality. The defensible finding is the fragility: there is no guard, no degradation path, and no CPU fallback, so a JIT-fusion fault renders the environment unrunnable on GPU rather than merely slower.

findings.title: Doc drift inside the subsystem: step() and ComposedActionSpace docstrings contradict the code, and the action-space one is load-bearing
findings.evidence: step()'s docstring says 'actions: [num_agents] tensor of actions (0-4)' against an action space of 8+. ComposedActionSpace's class docstring says 'substrate_action_count: Number from substrate (6 for Grid2D, 8 for Grid3D)', but grid2d.get_default_actions emits UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT (+4 diagonals when enabled) AND INTERACT AND WAIT as substrate actions (:167-300). This is not cosmetic: action_executor.py:143 computes `interact_mask = (actions == interact_action_idx) & substrate_mask` where substrate_mask = actions < substrate_action_count (:27). If the docstring were true and INTERACT sat outside the substrate range, interact_mask would be identically False and INTERACT would never fire. A reader who trusts the docstring will draw the wrong conclusion about the executor.

completeness.evidence: Six substrate families each implement all 14 abstract methods (base.py has 14 @abstractmethod; grid2d/grid3d/gridnd/continuous/continuousnd/aspatial all concrete), and the expression language is fully wired end-to-end into effects/compiler.py, items/manager.py, vfs/evaluator.py, vfs/vtc.py, vfs/profiles.py, universe/compilers/vfs.py. Everything every shipped pack actually uses works: I compiled and ran configs/default_curriculum (grid/square/relative/clamp, L0_0_minimal and L2_partial_observability), configs/test/gridnd_4d_pack, configs/test/effects_smoke — all OK. The holes are at the edges of the declared matrix: `type: grid3d` has no factory branch (factory.py:152 raises 'Unknown substrate type: grid3d'); `observation_encoding: scaled` crashes for grid and gridnd; `width != height` is rejected at vectorized_env.py:178-180 despite the compiler handling it (obs_grid_encoding correctly emitted as 48 for 8x6); `topology: cubic` + `active_vision: partial` crashes. Switch/Reduce AST nodes (ast_nodes.py:275,292) have no parser, evaluator, or type-checker path. world/types/primitive.py (128 LOC) has zero production consumers.

correctness.evidence: Four defects proven by execution, not inspection. (1) scaled encoding: `_encode_position_features` returns [N,4] (grid2d.py:434-441 -> _encode_scaled at grid2d.py:325-361) while compilers/observation.py:140 hardcodes position_dim=2 -> ValueError "Observation field 'obs_position' produced shape (4, 4), expected (4, 2)" at observation_encoder.py:106-109. Same on gridnd: shape (3,8) expected (3,4). (2) cubic + partial vision: Grid3D.encode_partial_observation (grid3d.py:554) returns a (2r+1)^3 cube = 125 dims while compilers/observation.py:110-114 computes a 2D window = 25 -> ValueError "produced (2, 125), expected (2, 25)". (3) grid3d literal declared at stratum_config.py:167 and branched on as live at observation.py:64,110,138 and metadata.py:110, but factory.py has no branch -> hard fail. (4) mypy error: action_mask_builder.py:21 imports `Substrate` from townlet.substrate.base, which only defines `SpatialSubstrate`. Also metadata.py:110-116 silently sets `grid_size = width`, discarding height. (The one failing test, test_distances.py::test_interaction_uses_substrate_distance, is a missing libnvrtc-builtins.so.13.0 on this host, not a code defect.)

correctness.evidence: PROVEN, not inferred. (1) LSTM training does no BPTT: `RecurrentSpatialQNetwork.forward` reads `self.hidden_state` (networks.py:271-272) and returns `new_hidden` but never assigns it; the training unroll at vectorized.py:777-783 calls `recurrent_network(batch['observations'][:, t, :])` with no `hidden=` argument and never calls `set_hidden_state`, so all seq_len steps start from the zeros written by `reset_hidden_state` at :777. I ran it: feeding the SAME observation at t=0..3 under the training-loop unroll gives `allclose(q[0], q[3]) == True`, while threading hidden explicitly gives False. The same defect repeats in the target unroll (:826-828) and both Double-DQN passes (:798-807). Rollout (:643-645) DOES thread hidden, so training and inference see different dynamics. (2) vectorized.py:898 calls `reset_hidden_state(batch_size=self.num_agents)` after every training step, wiping rollout memory mid-episode every `train_frequency` steps. (3) Last-timestep bootstrap: `if t < seq_len-1 ... else: q_target = batch['rewards'][:, t]` (:817-819, :837-839) treats the final index of every sampled subsequence as terminal, but `sample_sequences` picks arbitrary mid-episode offsets (sequential_replay_buffer.py:237) and the mask only zeroes steps AFTER a real terminal (:255-259) — so 1/seq_len of all recurrent targets are systematically wrong. (4) vectorized.py:688 takes `self.current_curriculum_decisions[0].depletion_multiplier` and applies agent 0's difficulty to the whole population, making per-agent `PerformanceTracker.agent_stages` inert for agents 1..N-1. (5) `_difficulty_to_stage` (vectorized.py:483-486) inverts assuming difficulty spans [0,1], but adversarial.py:364-369 maps into [min_difficulty, max_difficulty]; with the shipped 0.2/1.0 band, stage 1 -> 0.2 -> reported stage 2. (6) adversarial.py:101 computes `last_survival_rate = rewards / 100.0` with a magic 100 instead of `max_steps_per_episode`.

findings.title: LSTM is never unrolled during training — recurrent Q-learning silently trains a memoryless network
findings.evidence: `RecurrentSpatialQNetwork.forward` reads `hidden = self.hidden_state` (networks.py:271-272) and RETURNS `new_hidden` (:290) but never assigns it back. The training unroll calls `recurrent_network(batch['observations'][:, t, :])` with no `hidden=` argument and never calls `set_hidden_state`, so every one of the seq_len steps starts from the zeros written by `reset_hidden_state` at :777. Verified empirically: feeding the SAME observation at t=0..3 under the training-loop unroll yields `torch.allclose(q[0], q[3]) == True`; threading hidden explicitly yields False. The target unroll (:826-828) and both Double-DQN passes (:798-807) have the identical defect. Rollout (:643-645) DOES call set_hidden_state, so the policy is trained under one dynamics and executed under another. Compounding this, :898 calls `reset_hidden_state(batch_size=self.num_agents)` after every training step, wiping accumulated rollout memory mid-episode every `train_frequency` steps. Latent rather than live only because no shipped brain.yaml is `type: recurrent` — it fires the moment anyone authors the documented L2/L3 POMDP levels.

findings.title: Every sampled recurrent subsequence's final timestep is bootstrapped as terminal, corrupting 1/seq_len of all Q-targets
findings.evidence: Both the Double-DQN and vanilla branches do `if t < seq_len - 1: q_target = r + gamma*q_next*(~done) else: q_target = batch['rewards'][:, t]`. `sample_sequences` chooses `start_idx = random.randint(0, ep_len - seq_len)` (:237), so the final index is almost always mid-episode. The validity mask only zeroes steps AFTER a genuine terminal (:255-259) and never marks the final index as non-terminal, so those targets are included in the loss at full weight. Systematically biases values downward toward the immediate reward for a fixed fraction of every batch.

findings.title: Difficulty-to-stage inversion assumes a [0,1] band while the curriculum emits a configured band, corrupting stage telemetry

With the band shipped in every training.yaml (0.2/1.0), stage 1 -> difficulty 0.2 -> reported stage 2. (3) collections.py:20-23 raises ValueError('radius required') for `nearby_agents`, and nothing can supply radius from YAML, so the collection is a guaranteed runtime crash from any config. (4) compiler.py:390-397 parses and stores position_ast for non-literal spawn_item positions, but executor.py:243-273 only accepts 'self'/'target'/'random'/list/tuple and raises ValueError otherwise — a compile-time-accepted expression is a guaranteed runtime error; `position: null` (the schema default) also raises. (6) universe/compilers/effects.py:31-33 puts unprefixed `bar.{name}` in the type schema and context.py:243-248 set_path('bar.X') replaces the whole batched tensor, so a per-agent effect writing `modify: bar.energy` silently mutates every agent. keep_these: CommandCompiler's type checker and AST baker (src/townlet/effects/compiler.py, 411 lines). It validates every path against a real schema, checks value/target type agreement, and stores the compiled AST on the node so the executor never parses at runtime (executor.py:14 'No ExpressionParser import'). This is the single best piece of engineering in the subsystem and the reason config errors surface at compile time rather than in step 40,000.

Compile-time PARALLEL write-conflict detection (compiler.py:314-352): collect_writes recurses through nested blocks and raises if two branches target the same path. That is the correct, cheap way to make 'parallel' safe in a vectorized runtime, and it is exactly the kind of static guarantee a declarative substrate should offer.

Explicit refusal to support nested for_each (compiler.py:246-267) with the message 'Nested for_each is not supported under current vectorized constraints'. Refusing a feature loudly instead of shipping it half-working is the right call and should be preserved verbatim.

The bounded-resource discipline throughout: MAX_CASCADE_DEPTH=10 (executor.py:16) enforced at executor.py:192-194 with a clear infinite-loop message, MAX_COLLECTION_SIZE=256 enforced in both resolve_collection and _execute_for_each, MAX_DELAY_TICKS/MAX_SCHEDULED_ITEMS in scheduler.py:8-9. Effects can cascade without being able to hang training.

EffectCatalog.__post_init__ (catalog.py:44-48) building a deterministic sorted effect_name_to_id table so effects can be encoded into observation tensors with stable indices across runs and checkpoints. Small, correct, and load-bearing for reproducibility.

The four reapply policies (stack/renew/merge/replace) are fully implemented in EffectManager.spawn_effect (manager.py:130-200), including running on_interrupt with a distinguishing interrupt_reason ('merged_by_effect' / 'replaced_by_effect' / 'manually_cancelled') and cancelling the replaced instance's pending scheduled work before replacement (manager.py:167). Covered by tests/test_townlet/unit/effects/test_reapply_policies.py.
The `observable` flag is genuinely live: get_observable_agent_effects (manager.py:264-267) feeds effect observation slots at vectorized_env.py:903-916. Keep as-is.

ItemManager's fixed-size VFS slot pool (vfs_free_slots, manager.py:186) with allocate-on-spawn / release-on-despawn, and the O(1) _position_index (manager.py:277-283, 428-436, 478-486). Correct GPU-friendly resource management, and the position index avoids an O(n_items) scan per query.

Item identity preservation across pickup/drop: lift_item/place_item (items/manager.py:407-468) move the SAME instance between active_items and held_items without freeing the VFS slot, so durability and other per-instance state survive a drop. held_items are ticked and expire alongside active items (manager.py:557-585). This is the right model and it is tested end-to-end.

The exclusive-vs-shared item distinction, implemented consistently across InventoryState.add_item (inventory.py:113-115), lift_item (manager.py:422-424) and handle_drop_slot_action (action_handlers.py:376-382): shared items stay in the world while held. A genuinely thoughtful modelling decision.
InventoryState.purge_instance (inventory.py:196-210) called from despawn_item (manager.py:501) — a real memory-leak fix that clears both the slot tensor and the metadata dict.

tests/test_townlet/integration/test_items_integration.py as a whole. It is the one test in this subsystem that exercises the real config pack through the real environment and asserts on real numeric bar deltas (:146, :191, :234-237, :264-268). It is the template every other declarative subsystem needs.

findings.title: effects.yaml with a mismatched root key silently compiles to an EMPTY effect catalog
findings.evidence: EffectsConfig declares no model_config, so pydantic ignores unknown keys; version defaults to "1.0" and effect_definitions defaults to []. The loader does EffectsConfig(**yaml.safe_load(text)) with no wrapper. Executed: EffectsConfig(**yaml.safe_load(open('configs/reference/model_pack/effects.yaml'))) -> len(effect_definitions)==0, silently discarding the pack's only effect definition (`ate_food`). configs/test/vfs_bar_access/effects.yaml uses `effects: {version, active_effects: []}` — `active_effects` is not a schema field at all — and is likewise accepted as empty. Two CLAUDE.md no-defaults violations (a defaulted version and a defaulted required list) are what convert a one-line typo into silent behaviour loss. Note the inconsistency that invites the typo: items.yaml REQUIRES an `items:` wrapper (items_config.py:263 reads data['items']) while effects.yaml requires its absence.

findings.title: Item- and affordance-scoped effects never tick, never expire, and leak permanently
findings.evidence: EffectManager.tick iterates self.global_effects (line 376) and self.agent_effects (line 383) only. self.item_effects and self.affordance_effects are populated by _add_to_scope (lines 249-260) and read by get_all_active_effects/cancel_effect, but are never ticked or reaped. Executed proof: spawning one ITEM-scoped and one AFFORDANCE-scoped effect (duration=2) with on_tick `modify: bar.energy - 0.1`, then calling manager.tick four times, left energy at 1.0 unchanged and both instances still reporting duration_remaining=2. configs/test/items_smoke/effects.yaml ships four `scope: item` effects (wear_and_tear, item_degradation, item_break, food_decay) with on_tick pipelines that can never run — a shipped non-default value for an inert field.

findings.title: spawn_effect hardcodes scope=AGENT, so the `scope:` field in effects.yaml never reaches the runtime
findings.evidence: EffectManager.spawn_effect has exactly one caller in src/townlet — executor._execute_spawn_effect (grep verified; the other hits are NullEffectManager stubs at items/action_handlers.py:23, effects/context.py:16, environment/affordance_engine.py:571). Line 220 carries the comment 'Note: scope hardcoded to AGENT for now (can extend later)'. CompiledEffect.scope is faithfully carried from YAML through catalog.py:90 and then read by nothing at spawn time. Combined with the tick gap above, three of the four documented EffectScope values are unreachable AND unexecutable.

findings.title: spawn_interval and spawn_position are documented as the item respawn mechanism and have zero consumers
findings.evidence: grep across src/townlet finds no read of rule.spawn_interval or rule.spawn_position — only the field definitions and a stale comment at environment/vectorized_env.py:1078. despawn_item queues a respawn ONLY inside `if schedule is not None and isinstance(schedule, SpawnScheduleConfig)`; the else branch is `pass` ('No schedule: do not queue respawns automatically'). Every appearance example in docs/config-schemas/items.md uses spawn_interval, so an author following the documentation gets zero respawns and no error. Both fields carry defaults, so the config never even has to be typed. Per zero-BC these should be deleted, not deprecated.

findings.title: Item interactions.on_drop is validated and compiled but never executed
findings.evidence: on_drop commands are parsed to AST and type-compiled into CompiledItemType.compiled_on_drop, and _execute_interaction has a dispatch branch for it (action_handlers.py:93-94), but no caller in src/townlet ever passes interaction='on_drop'. handle_drop_slot_action removes the slot entry and calls place_item without touching Effects. Any author-written on_drop pipeline validates, type-checks, and silently does nothing.

findings.title: Global-scoped effects are reaped without running on_despawn
findings.evidence: The global tick loop calls _tick_effect then `self.global_effects.pop(i)` directly, bypassing _despawn_effect (manager.py:511) which is what executes on_despawn and cancels scheduled work. The agent loop at lines 383-397 correctly calls _despawn_effect. Executed proof: a global-scoped effect with an on_despawn `modify` expired after its duration and the bar was unchanged. Any 'reversal on expiry' semantics (the documented use for on_despawn, effects.md:511) silently fails at global scope.

findings.title: `for_each: nearby_agents` is a guaranteed runtime crash from any YAML config
findings.evidence: _resolve_nearby_agents raises ValueError('radius required for nearby_agents collection') when radius is None. executor.py:449 passes radius=command.radius. CommandNode.radius is only ever None from config: CommandConfig has no radius field (and extra='forbid' prevents adding one), and CommandParser.parse_command never sets it (parser.py:79-96). The compiler ACCEPTS `for_each: nearby_agents` (compiler.py:277-279 only checks the name is a known resolver), so this compiles cleanly and crashes on first execution. Separately, EffectManager.tick is called from vectorized_env.py:1013 WITHOUT agent_positions, so nearby_agents would fail in on_tick even with a radius. Proven live-but-unauthorable by tests/test_townlet/integration/test_aoe_effects.py:37-46 which sets radius=5.0 on the CommandNode from Python.

findings.title: spawn_item accepts a position expression at compile time and raises at runtime; position=None (the schema default) also raises
findings.evidence: compiler.py:394-397 parses, type-checks and stores position_ast for any position string outside {'random','self','target'}. executor._execute_spawn_item never reads position_ast; it dispatches on the literal strings and list/tuple, then falls through to `raise ValueError(f'Invalid position: {command.position}')` (line 272). CommandConfig.position defaults to None, which hits the same raise. A compile-clean config crashes on first execution — the worst possible ordering for a declarative product.

findings.title: `delay` commands issued from affordance stages are scheduled into the past and stranded forever
findings.evidence: _execute_delay passes base_tick=context.current_tick to Scheduler.schedule, giving due = base_tick + delay_ticks. affordance_engine.py:205 passes current_tick=None for the on_start stage (context defaults to 0), and line 250 documents per_tick's current_tick as the affordance's PROGRESS tick in [0, duration_ticks-1] — not the global tick. Scheduler.advance is driven by env global_tick (vectorized_env.py:1013) and drain_due (scheduler.py:70-72) pops only pending[current_tick] exactly, never sweeping past-due entries. So once global_tick exceeds the affordance-relative due tick, the entry sits in scheduler.pending forever, consuming the MAX_SCHEDULED_ITEMS budget and silently never running.

findings.title: The repository's only YAML spawn_effect example fails schema validation
findings.evidence: The model pack writes `- spawn_effect: {effect_id: ate_food, target: agent, intensity: self.vfs.calories}` (nested mapping). CommandConfig.spawn_effect is `str | None`. Executed: CommandConfig(**cmd) raises ValidationError 'spawn_effect: Input should be a valid string'. Even corrected to the flat form, `target: agent` is not self/target/int so the parser routes it to the expression path (parser.py:38-46) where the compiler demands an int-typed expression, and `intensity: self.vfs.calories` cannot be a float. The pack is unverified — it does not compile at all today (actions.yaml raises extra_forbidden on custom_actions.0.costs/effects).

findings.title: Unprefixed `bar.X` is in the effects type schema, so a per-agent effect can silently mutate the whole batch
findings.evidence: build_schema emits both `bar.{name}` and `target.bar.{name}`. set_path('bar.X') does `self.bars[bar_name] = value`, replacing the whole [batch] tensor, which the environment then writes back wholesale (vectorized_env.py:1022-1023). _execute_modify broadcasts a scalar result to the original shape first (executor.py:168-169), so `modify: bar.energy / value: bar.energy - 0.1` inside an effect attached to agent 3 drains EVERY agent. Nothing in the schema, compiler or docs distinguishes the batch-wide form from the per-entity `target.bar.*` form. This is also what makes the _execute_if `.any()` collapse (executor.py:400-410) reachable: with `target.` prefixes the condition always indexes to a scalar, so the vectorized ambiguity only bites for unprefixed paths.

findings.title: GET matches item position by exact tuple equality while custom verbs use a float tolerance
findings.evidence: handle_get_action does `if active_item.position == agent_pos_tuple`. _positions_match exists a few lines above with a docstring explaining that 'Continuous substrates keep fractional coordinates; rounding them to ints breaks equality checks' — and it is applied to handle_custom_action (line 337) and compute_custom_action_masks (line 292) but not to GET. On a continuous substrate, custom local verbs work and GET cannot. handle_get_action also linearly scans active_items instead of using the O(1) _position_index built for exactly this purpose (items/manager.py:277-283).

findings.title: Scheduler state is never checkpointed; state_dict/load_state_dict have zero callers
findings.evidence: grep for state_dict/load_state_dict across src/townlet and tests finds no reference to the Scheduler methods anywhere — not even in tests/test_townlet/unit/effects/test_scheduler.py. Pending delayed commands are therefore lost across checkpoint save/resume, silently changing behaviour on restore. state_dict also returns a live reference to self.pending rather than a copy, so a caller mutating the returned dict corrupts the scheduler.

findings.title: Dead code and duplicated fallback shims across the subsystem
findings.location: src/townlet/effects/manager.py:552 (_build_context); src/townlet/effects/schema.py:125-146 (EffectDefinition); src/townlet/effects/manager.py:600 (cancel_effect); src/townlet/effects/context.py:15,20; src/townlet/items/action_handlers.py:20; src/townlet/environment/affordance_engine.py:570; src/townlet/environment/null_managers.py

findings.title: Effect intensity and spawn-site duration cannot be expressions or overrides from config

findings.title: No-defaults principle violations concentrated in the newest schema fields

completeness.evidence: Live inference IS complete end-to-end: unified_server.py:401-409 constructs LiveInferenceServer, live_inference.py:633-793 runs episodes, :795-909 broadcasts. But three whole capabilities are built and unreachable. (1) Recording: runner.py:519-534 constructs EpisodeRecorder when recording.enabled, yet recorder.py:242-263 can never return True with any shipped config (proved below). (2) Replay: LiveInferenceServer only builds a ReplayManager when db_path AND recordings_dir are both passed (live_inference.py:146-154); unified_server.py:401-409 passes neither, and live_inference.py:1240-1258 (__main__) calls run_server without them, so no caller in the repo can reach replay mode — while frontend/src has zero occurrences of 'replay' or 'recording'. (3) Frontend orchestration: unified_server.py:34-40 docstring advertises 'Frontend Subprocess: runs npm run dev' as component 3, and _start_frontend (unified_server.py:441-520, ~80 LOC) plus _stop_frontend (:522-546) exist, but grep shows ZERO callers of either.
